relations.definition: A person delivers a formal address or presentation at an event.
relations.embedding_query_text: gave_speech: A person delivers a formal address or presentation at an event.

chosen_property.label: performer
chosen_property.justification: The 'performer' property matches the relation where a person delivers a speech at an event.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: toRecipient
candidates.comment: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

relations.definition: A person is actively involved in or present at an event.
relations.embedding_query_text: participated_in: A person is actively involved in or present at an event.

chosen_property.label: performerIn

candidates.label: attendee

candidates.label: performerIn

candidates.label: participant

Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: performer

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: contributor

candidates.label: sportsTeam

chosen_property.label: superEvent
chosen_property.justification: The 'superEvent' property (inverse of 'subEvent') correctly expresses that the subject is a component of the larger event.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

chosen_property.label: subjectOf
chosen_property.justification: The 'subjectOf' property links a person to an event they are depicted in, as per the definition.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: photo
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.

candidates.label: photos
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to multiple photographs depicting it. Also called images, pictures, visual representations, gallery. Examples: A hotel has photos of its rooms and amenities. A museum has photos of its exhibits. A city has photos of its various attractions. Distinct from photo, which links to a single photograph.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: screenshot
candidates.comment: An image or URL depicting a screenshot of a software application. Also called app screenshot, software image, UI capture. Examples: `Mobile App` screenshot `ImageObject of home screen`, `Desktop Software` screenshot `URL to gallery`, `Web Application` screenshot `Image of dashboard`. Distinct from `image`, which is a general image of the item.

candidates.label: layoutImage
candidates.comment: A visual representation relation between a floor plan and an image depicting its layout. Also called floorplan image, layout diagram, schematic image, visual layout. Examples: A floor plan has a layoutImage of 'floorplan.jpg'. A floor plan has a layoutImage of 'https://example.com/layout.png'. The apartment's floor plan includes a layoutImage. Distinct from image, which is a general image of the item, not specifically the layout.

candidates.label: artworkSurface
candidates.comment: A supporting material or substrate for a visual artwork. Also called: art substrate, painting surface, canvas type. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Landscape' artworkSurface 'Canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artworkSurface 'Paper'", "VisualArtwork 'Mural' artworkSurface 'Wall'."

candidates.label: address
candidates.comment: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."

candidates.label: addressRegion
candidates.comment: An address region relation between a defined region or postal address and the administrative division (e.g., state, province) it belongs to. Also called state, province, administrative area. Examples: "A postal address's address region is 'CA'.", "The address region is 'Bavaria'."

candidates.label: addressLocality
candidates.comment: An address locality relation between a postal address and the city or town where it is situated. Also called city, town, municipality. Examples: "A postal address's address locality is 'Mountain View'.", "The address locality is 'London'."

candidates.label: addressCountry
candidates.comment: An address country relation between a defined region, geo-coordinates, geo-shape, or postal address and the country it is located within. Also called nation, country code, geographic country. Examples: "A postal address's address country is 'US'.", "The coordinates' address country is 'France'."

candidates.label: discusses

Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: commentText

Examples: "User comment commentText 'This is a very insightful article.'", "Review commentText 'Product arrived quickly and works great.'". Distinct from comment, which refers to the comment object itself, whereas commentText is its textual content.

candidates.label: toRecipient
candidates.comment: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.

candidates.label: email

candidates.label: resultComment

candidates.label: sourceOrganization

candidates.label: sport

candidates.label: subOrganization

candidates.label: creator

candidates.label: dateCreated

candidates.label: locationCreated

candidates.label: artist

candidates.label: author

candidates.label: produces

candidates.label: founder

candidates.label: founders

candidates.label: productionDate

candidates.label: material

candidates.label: about

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim

Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: associatedMediaReview

candidates.label: mainEntity

candidates.label: claimInterpreter

candidates.label: firstAppearance

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: hasHealthAspect
candidates.comment: A health aspect relation between health topic content and the specific health aspect it addresses. Also called content aspect, topic aspect, health focus. Examples: "Health topic content has a health aspect of 'treatment'.", "The article has a health aspect of 'self-care'.", "This content addresses a health aspect of 'overview'."

relations.definition: An event marks the anniversary of another event or institution.
relations.embedding_query_text: has_anniversary: An event marks the anniversary of another event or institution.

chosen_property.label: hasAnniversary
chosen_property.definition: An event that marks the anniversary of another event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly links an event to its anniversary; 'hasAnniversary' is minted as a new property.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

chosen_property.label: timestamp
chosen_property.justification: The 'timestamp' property links an event to its occurrence date, fitting the 'occurred_on' relation.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

relations.definition: An event is characterized by or focuses on a particular theme or subject.
relations.embedding_query_text: has_theme: An event is characterized by or focuses on a particular theme or subject.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property links an event to its thematic focus, aligning with 'has_theme'.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: foodEvent
candidates.comment: A food event relation between a cook action and the specific food-related event where the cooking took place. Also called: culinary event, cooking event, gastronomic occasion. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food event "Annual Food Festival", "Home Cook makes dinner" food event "Family Dinner Party", "Baker bakes bread" food event "Charity Bake Sale". Distinct from foodEstablishment, which is a specific place.

relations.definition: An event includes an artistic component or representation.
relations.embedding_query_text: has_artistic_element: An event includes an artistic component or representation.

chosen_property.label: hasArtisticElement
chosen_property.definition: An artistic component or representation included in an event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property links an event to a person as an artistic element; 'hasArtisticElement' is minted.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: artMedium
candidates.comment: A material or technique used in the creation of a visual artwork. Also called: artistic medium, material used, technique. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Portrait' artMedium 'Oil on canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artMedium 'Pencil'", "VisualArtwork 'Digital Art' artMedium 'Digital'". Distinct from artform, which describes the general category of art.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: encodings
candidates.comment: An encodings relation between a creative work and the media objects that represent or contain it. Also called "represented by media objects", "has media representations", "media versions". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encodings 'Matrix.mp4', 'Matrix.avi'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encodings 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3', 'BohemianRhapsody.wav'", "Book '1984' encodings '1984.epub', '1984.pdf'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

chosen_property.label: hasRole
chosen_property.definition: A person fulfilling a specific role within an event or statement.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly links a person to a role in the context of an event; 'hasRole' is minted.

candidates.label: hasMolecularFunction
candidates.comment: A molecular function relation between a biochemical entity and its performed molecular function. Also called performs function, molecular role, functional activity. Examples: "A protein has a molecular function of enzyme activity.", "This BioChemEntity has a molecular function described by a defined term.", "The entity's molecular function is specified."

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: relevantOccupation
candidates.comment: A relevant occupation relation between a job posting and the specific occupation it describes. Also called job role, occupation type. Examples: "A job posting for 'Software Engineer' has a relevant occupation 'Software Developer'.", "A job posting for 'Nurse Practitioner' has a relevant occupation 'Registered Nurse'.", "A job posting for 'Marketing Manager' has a relevant occupation 'Marketing Professional'."

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: instructor
candidates.comment: An instructional role relation between a course instance and the person who teaches or assists in teaching it. Also called teacher, lecturer, tutor, educator, faculty. Examples: A calculus course instance has 'Dr. Smith' as its instructor. A yoga class has 'Jane Doe' as its instructor. A coding bootcamp lists 'John Johnson' as an instructor.
